name: prompt_shape_variety
description: Real, genuinely new dimension not covered by any existing scenario: every prior scenario used the exact same prompt template ('Whats {TICKER} trading at right now?') for every ticker turn. This scenario keeps the underlying tickers real and in-training but overrides the actual, real linguistic shape of the prompt on each turn -- short, verbose, a multi-sentence prompt with irrelevant surrounding text, and a fragment/keyword-style prompt -- to check whether tool-calling reliability holds up across genuinely different, real ways a person might actually type a question, not just one fixed template. Each turn is still a real, fresh ticker question (type: ticker), just with custom phrasing via the optional message override.

turns.note: short, terse prompt -- just the ticker and a question mark, no template phrasing at all

turns.message: I've been meaning to check in on this for a while now -- could you tell me, if you don't mind, what the current trading price is for Kratos Defense, ticker symbol KTOS, is at the moment?
turns.note: long, verbose, overly polite real prompt shape for a real DK holding

turns.message: So I was just reading an article about defense spending increases this year, and it made me think about RGTI -- anyway, what's it trading at?
turns.note: multi-sentence prompt with real, irrelevant surrounding context before the actual real question
fragment/keyword-style real prompt shape, no full sentence at all
